title: AI-assisted study finds limited code sharing in clinical prediction research
summary: An AI-assisted empirical review found code-sharing statements in 482 of 3,967 clinical prediction studies (12.2%) and assessed 380 repositories. GPT-5.2 screened papers, extracted links and characterized repository features; human reviewers checked 500 papers and 35 repositories. The sample covered studies citing TRIPOD or TRIPOD+AI that were accessible through PubMed Central Open Access, so it does not represent all clinical research. Automated errors remain possible, and repository features do not establish executable reproducibility. The journal article was published October 9, before the November 19 MIT announcement.
organization: Dana-Farber Cancer Institute; Massachusetts Institute of Technology

evidence.unknown: Selection and classification error limit generalization; actual reproducibility was not established.
evidence.ai_role: LLM performs screening, link extraction and structured feature assessment.

source_review.scope: Institution-deposited publisher PDF: bounded results, Methods and limitations; publisher indexed text and PubMed/institutional publication-date metadata. Direct publisher route blocked; no code executed.
